answer: The chain runs in six stages, each one reducing the product to something the next stage can handle. (1) Radix digits (page vub): each n-bit integer is written as q = ceil(n/b) digits in radix 2^b, with b = ceil(log2 n). The digit product is a wrap-around product (the wiki's totipuv) of length S, and S is long enough that nothing wraps and every coefficient fits in 3b bits, so the integer product becomes a totipuv of short coefficients. (2) Address map (page guf): S is a product of pairwise coprime lengths s_1..s_d. The map sending x to the product of x_i raised to mu_i is an isomorphism that preserves totipuv, so the single length-S totipuv becomes a d-axis one, with one axis per s_i. This is needed because the later stages act on one axis at a time. (3) Resampling and chirps (pages roz and pap): a transform of prime length s is re-expressed through a transform of a nearby power-of-two length t, so only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm. For even t_i the chirp identity gives Q F_t u = conj(a) times (a totipuv (conj(a) times u)) divided by T, so the target reordering is absorbed into an ordinary totipuv of power-of-two length T, between two pointwise phase multiplications. (4) Twist (page taf, with page reb): the last cyclic axis is turned into the ring R_r = C[y]/(y^r+1) by multiplying entry k by zeta^k with zeta = e^(pi i/r). The wrap sign of ring multiplication then reproduces the totipuv on that axis. This is needed because in R_r multiplying by a power of y is only a signed shift, so the transforms over the ring need no complex multiplications. (5) Synthetic-transform convolution (pages tab and gip): both operands are transformed over R_r with roots of unity omega_t = y^(2r/t), multiplied record by record in the ring, and transformed back, with a scaling by the number of records. (6) Assembly and rounding (page siz): after the two forward transforms, the pointwise product, the opposite transform, a rescaling by S, and multiplication by 2^(2b+4) S, the values are rounded to integers, mapped back by the inverse address map, and carries are propagated to give the exact 2n-bit product. Rounding is exact because the error is below 1/2, a claim the page cites to another page that I did not open. Confidence is moderate: I could follow the stage-by-stage reductions and their size bookkeeping, but I took the error bounds and the cited lemmas on trust.

key_idea.statement: The integer product is cut into digits, turned into a wrap-around product of short coefficients, computed through transforms whose twiddle multiplications are cheap, and then rounded back to exact integers.
